papers.title_en: ACAM-J-MARS: Multi-Atlas Riemannian Spectral Representations for Decoding Advanced Meditation States from fMRI
papers.authors: Jian Wang, Winson F. Z. Yang, Wugeng Zheng, Matthew D. Sacchet
papers.evidence: 使用多图谱黎曼谱表示从fMRI解码冥想状态
papers.tldr: 针对fMRI解码高级冥想状态的困难，提出ACAM-J-MARS多图谱黎曼谱表示，利用多图谱功能连接、SPD矩阵黎曼流形与对数欧氏切空间投影，并结合低频BOLD频谱能量，在22名实践者数据上提升分类性能，早期vs晚期准确率0.757，三分类0.545，较最强基线提升10.8个百分点。
papers.abstract_en: Inferring jhana-type advanced concentration absorption meditation (ACAM-J) states from fMRI data is challenging due to the spatially distributed nature of meditation-related effects, substantial inter-individual variability that can exceed within-subject state differences, and limited sample sizes. Conventional machine-learning approaches often formulate this problem as unimodal, Euclidean, atlas-based classification, thereby neglecting the non-Euclidean geometry of functional connectivity matrices and underrepresenting temporal information in functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI); these limitations can lead to suboptimal classification performance. We propose ACAM-J-MARS (\textbf{M}ulti-\textbf{A}tlas \textbf{R}iemannian \textbf{S}pectral representation), which computes functional connectivity using multiple atlases, represents symmetric positive definite (SPD) connectivity matrices on a Riemannian manifold, projects them into a log-Euclidean tangent space, and augments connectivity-derived features with low-frequency BOLD spectral energy to better resolve subtle state differences under heterogeneous variability. Evaluated on 204 segments from 22 practitioners, ACAM-J-MARS improves performance across multiple backbone models, achieving a balanced accuracy of 0.757 for early versus late ACAM-J classification and 0.545 for three-class classification, corresponding to a 10.8-point absolute improvement over the strongest baseline. These findings suggest that the proposed representation improves the decoding of advanced meditative brain states and may enable downstream applications such as closed-loop neurofeedback and real-time psychophysiological brain-computer interfaces.

papers.title_en: A Multi-Layer Navigation System for Smart Wheelchairs with a Limited Input Interface
papers.authors: Piero Simonetto, Anna Polato, Francesco Pasti, Muhammad Rameez ur Rahman, Sebastiano Vascon, Nicola Bellotto, Emanuele Menegatti, Stefano Tortora, Luca Tonin
papers.evidence: 用于智能轮椅导航的脑机接口
papers.tldr: 针对智能轮椅在未知环境导航和用户意图理解中的挑战，本文提出多层导航系统MLNS，结合虚拟传感器驱动势场法进行障碍物检测、模型预测控制生成轨迹、开放词汇视觉识别目标，并通过优先队列选择目标。在真实智能轮椅上经10名参与者验证，系统在有限错误输入下仍鲁棒有效，展示辅助技术应用潜力。
papers.abstract_en: Smart wheelchairs are robotic devices that gather information from the surroundings and allow people to safely drive through various environments. They usually rely on the interpretation of high-level user's intentions, typically decoded through human-robot interface (HRI) or brain-machine interface (BMI). However, navigating in an unknown environment and accurately understanding user commands remain significant challenges. Misinterpretation of commands or the environment can lead to user frustration, distrust of the system, or even unsafe situations. In this paper, we present a novel Multi-Layer Navigation System (MLNS) for a smart wheelchair that enables navigation in unknown environments while interpreting and safely contextualizing user's intentions even in the case of limited and faulty commands. The stack relies on a Virtual Sensors-Driven Potential Fields (ViSPF) method for obstacle detection that accounts for the wheelchair's actual size, a Model Predictive Control (MPC) module for trajectory generation, and an open-vocabulary computer vision algorithm for target identification. Finally, a system based on Priority Queue (PQ) was implemented for target selection. We validated our system on a real smart wheelchair with experiments involving 10 participants without disabilities, including scenarios with faulty input interfaces. The results demonstrate the robustness and effectiveness of our system in real-world environments, proving its potential for practical applications in assistive technologies.

papers.title_en: Every route counts, but some count more: a max-plus view of the C. elegans brain
papers.authors: Emma Reyner-Fuentes, Sebastian Rudolph, Carmen Peláez-Moreno, Francisco J. Valverde-Albacete
papers.evidence: 神经信号路由的max-plus代数模型
papers.tldr: 该研究针对传统连接组分析将所有路径求和并置于欧几里得空间、模糊反馈回路的问题，提出用 max-plus 代数将神经信号视为路由而非扩散，信号沿路径累积且最强路径胜出。通过构建秀丽隐杆线虫功能连接组的时间变化多层模型（电、突触、单胺能、神经肽能、激素），分析五个网络，发现每个网络坍缩为少数主导反馈环，恢复了已知回路并指出新候选。结果表明基于序的描述保留生物学意义，脑状态可能存在于格而非欧几里得空间。
papers.abstract_en: Brains do not simply add up every signal they receive: they select which routes dominate. Yet connectomes are usually analyzed with tools that sum over all paths and place neural states in Euclidean spaces, blurring the feedback circuits that may sustain internal states. Here we treat neural signaling as routing instead of diffusion and describe it with max-plus algebra, in which signals accumulate along a path and the strongest route prevails. We propose a model in which the functional connectome of Caenorhabditis elegans emerges from the time-varying combination of electrical, synaptic, monoaminergic, neuropeptidergic and hormonal layers, and analyze five networks within this framework. Each collapses onto a handful of dominant feedback loops, which recover well-characterized circuits and point to new candidates for experimental study. Unlike linear spectra, these structures keep the biological meaning of the data, and their order-based description suggests that brain states live in lattices rather than Euclidean spaces.

papers.title_en: Beyond Low-Pass Dynamics: Frequency-Selective Spiking Reservoirs with Resonant Neurons
papers.authors: Aurora Micheli, Claudio Gallicchio, Nergis Tomen
papers.evidence: 谐振神经元脉冲储备池用于时间频率选择性
papers.tldr: 现有脉冲储备池计算多依赖LIF神经元，其低通动态难以区分不同时间频率编码。本文提出HRF-Res，用异质谐波共振-发放神经元替代LIF，赋予储备池频率选择性动态，提升表征判别力和分类精度。在十个基准上取得脉冲储备池方法领先精度，能耗比非脉冲振荡储备池最高降低19倍。
papers.abstract_en: Spiking reservoir computing combines the training efficiency of fixed recurrent reservoirs with the energy efficiency of event-driven inference, where computation is triggered by sparse spikes rather than executed densely at every timestep. However, existing spiking reservoirs almost exclusively rely on Leaky Integrate-and-Fire (LIF) neurons, whose low-pass dynamics limit their ability to distinguish information encoded at different temporal frequencies. We introduce HRF-Res, a liquid state machine in which LIF neurons are replaced by a heterogeneous population of Harmonic Resonate-and-Fire (HRF) neurons. These neurons exhibit intrinsic oscillatory dynamics and selectively respond to input frequencies, enabling the reservoir to capture frequency-specific temporal patterns. The result is more discriminative representations and higher classification accuracy than LIF-based reservoirs, achieved without sacrificing the energy efficiency of spiking computation, with up to 19x lower energy consumption than an equivalent non-spiking oscillatory reservoir. Evaluated on ten benchmarks spanning time series, sequential images, audio spike trains, and neuromorphic vision, HRF-Res achieves state-of-the-art accuracy among spiking reservoir methods. These results demonstrate that introducing frequency-selective dynamics into spiking reservoirs improves representational quality and classification performance while preserving their inherent energy efficiency.

papers.title_en: REVBRAIN: Real-time Probabilistic EEG Forecasting Using Residual Vector Quantization
papers.authors: Hanna Pankka, Jaakko Lehtinen, Timo Roine
papers.evidence: 用于脑状态依赖刺激的实时概率EEG预测
papers.tldr: 针对脑状态依赖刺激等应用需要实时EEG预测，现有WaveNet虽准确但推理速度过慢。本文提出REVBRAIN，利用残差向量量化将输出空间标记化，一次性生成整个预测窗口，在alpha频段200ms预测中实现笔记本GPU实时推理，速度比WaveNet快50倍以上且精度更高，为将概率EEG预测集成到BCI应用开辟新途径。
papers.abstract_en: Real-time forecasting of resting-state EEG signals is required by applications like brain-state-dependent stimulation, where computer generated actions are coupled with ongoing neural oscillations. Recently, the deep learning model WaveNet was proposed for the forecasting task. It shows superior accuracy compared to the prevailing method, the linear autoregressive (AR) model, and provides a built-in uncertainty measure due to its probabilistic modeling framework. However, inference using WaveNet is too slow for real-time use due to its sample-by-sample autoregressive operation: a single forecast requires evaluating the model tens or hundreds of times depending on the length of the prediction window.   In this paper, we present REVBRAIN, a probabilistic deep learning method that produces forecasts in real time by generating the forecast over the whole prediction horizon at once. This is achieved by tokenizing the output space using residual vector quantization (RVQ) and generating forecasts over the items in the tokenized space.   We tested REVBRAIN for forecasting 200 ms of EEG time series in the alpha-frequency band (8-13 Hz) and compared our results against WaveNet model. We found that REVBRAIN achieved real-time inference on a laptop GPU and an over $50\times$ speedup compared to WaveNet, while reaching superior prediction accuracy.   By achieving real-time inference speed, REVBRAIN enables incorporating accurate and probabilistic EEG forecasting into BCI applications, opening up new ways for investigating the functioning of the human brain.

papers.title_en: Optimal Neural Estimation for High-Dimensional Nonparametric Regression under Multisource Covariate Shift
papers.authors: Chenghao Xu, Haotian Xu, Shivam Kumar, Daren Wang
papers.evidence: 多源协变量偏移回归作为域适应方法
papers.tldr: 本文研究多源协变量偏移下的高维非参数回归，提出oracle加权神经网络估计器，证明其达到minimax最优速率（至对数因子），有效样本量由各源样本量、噪声方差和协变量偏移共同决定；并开发无需源噪声方差与偏移参数的自适应方法，在适当条件下达到同样最优速率。
papers.abstract_en: We study high-dimensional nonparametric regression under multisource covariate shift, where $\mathrm J$ sources of training data share a common regression function but differ in their covariate distributions, sample sizes, and noise variances. Our goal is to combine these sources to estimate the regression function accurately under a target covariate distribution. We propose an oracle weighted neural estimator and establish its minimax optimality up to logarithmic factors through matching upper and lower bounds. The resulting rate is $\mathsf n_{\rm eff}^{-2p/(2p+K)}$, where $p$ and $K$ denote the effective smoothness and dimension of the regression function, and the effective sample size is \begin{align} \mathsf n_{\rm eff} =\sum_{j=1}^{\mathrm J} \frac{n_j}{(1+σ_{ρ,j})σ_{ε,j}^{2}}. \nonumber \end{align} Here, $n_j$ is the sample size of source $j$, $σ_{ε,j}^{2}$ is its noise variance, and $σ_{ρ,j}$ controls the deviation between the covariate distribution of source $j$ and the target covariate distribution. We also develop an adaptive procedure that requires no knowledge of source noise variances or covariate-shift parameters. Under suitable conditions, this procedure attains the oracle minimax rate up to logarithmic factors.
